newsitem.title: CHINA: Hopewell still seeking Thai rail finance.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell still seeking Thai rail finance.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd is working with bankers to find a financing solution for its US$3.2 billion Bangkok mass transit system and has received no formal deadline from the Thai government, said a company spokeswoman on Friday.
"Hopewell is aware of the fact that the government would like to propose solutions to BERTS (Bangkok Elevated Rail Transport System) by the end of the month," said the Hopewell spokeswoman.
"This deadline is self-imposed and not on Hopewell. Hopewell has not received any formal notice of governmental deadline nor notice on the project," she said.

Sathien Wongvichien, Thailand's Deputy Permanent Secretary for Transport and Communications, said on July 24 that if Hopewell could not come up with a firm financing package by the end of July, the ministry could exercise its contractual right to scrap the 30-year BERTS operating concession awarded to Hopewell in 1990.
"Hopewell has been working on a financial solution to the Bangkok project with the bank group and will update the government on the progress," said the spokeswoman.
Nothing had changed for the company and Hopewell remained committed to the Bangkok project, the spokeswoman added.
